title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Titanium (Ti, Z=22) is 47.867(1)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Titanium (Ti, Z=22) as 47.867(1), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 22, symbol Ti, as Titanium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Titanium as 47.867(1). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: Ti-46 relative atomic mass 45.95262772(35), isotopic composition 0.0825(3); Ti-47 relative atomic mass 46.95175879(38), isotopic composition 0.0744(2); Ti-48 relative atomic mass 47.94794198(38), isotopic composition 0.7372(3); Ti-49 relative atomic mass 48.94786568(39), isotopic composition 0.0541(2); Ti-50 relative atomic mass 49.94478689(39), isotopic composition 0.0518(2). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
